title: Optimization Config diff view (risk highlighting + expected impact callouts)
text:
Optimization Config diff view (risk highlighting + expected impact callouts)

body:
Problem
Operators need to understand what changed between Optimization Config versions quickly and safely. The diff view must:
- Make it obvious which fields changed, at what scope (tenant/model/region), and whether the change is risky.
- Provide “expected impact” guidance to support go/no-go decisions before canary/promote.
- Reduce mistakes during incidents (when folks are stressed) and speed up rollback decisions.

Context
This ticket covers the Console UI design for the Optimization Config diff visualization used from:
- Version history timeline (select two versions → View diff)
- Safe apply flow (review changes before canary / promote)
- Rollback flow (review what you’re rolling back from/to)

Non-goals (v1)
- Full “git-style” multi-file/transactional diff across unrelated subsystems.
- Auto-suggesting config values.
- Explaining model-level architecture details; keep it operator-focused.

Users / personas
1) On-call SRE / Platform operator
- Needs fast risk read, confirmation of blast radius, and clear rollback-to-baseline confidence.

2) Customer admin (Dedicated/Private)
- Needs understandable explanation of what will impact latency/cost and where.

3) Applied ML / Quantization owner
- Needs quant profile changes called out with quality gate implications.

Design goals
- Skimmable first (summary + risk), deep details second (per-field diff).
- “What changed?” and “So what?” appear above the fold.
- Clearly show scope to prevent mis-scoped applies (tenant/model/region).
- Consistent semantics across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Information architecture
Diff page layout (recommended)
1) Header: “Optimization Config Diff”
- From: Version X (timestamp, author, label e.g., ‘candidate’, ‘promoted’)
- To: Version Y
- Scope chips: Tenant, Model, Region (and Environment where applicable)
- Status tags if version is Active / Canary / Rolled back-from

2) Summary strip (above the fold)
- Change summary counts: “3 high risk • 2 medium • 7 low • 1 informational”
- “Expected impact” callouts (generated by validation/semantics service when available):
  - Latency: “p95 risk ↑” / “likely neutral” / “unknown”
  - Error rate: “potential 5xx risk” if incompatible toggles
  - Cost: “tokens/sec efficiency likely ↑” where batching increases
  - Quality: only show for quantization profile changes (or mention “not applicable”)
- Prominent warning if a change touches a “stop-ship” field (see Risk model)

3) Risky changes section (pinned)
- A filtered list of fields marked High/Medium risk (expandable)
- Each item shows:
  - Field name + path
  - Old → New
  - Risk tag + short explanation
  - Link to learn more / runbook (contextual)

4) Full diff section
- Grouped by category: Batching, Caching, Quantization, Routing/Other
- Collapsible groups, default expand for groups with changes
- Each field row has:
  - Field label (human friendly) + JSON path (copyable)
  - Inline diff (old/new)
  - Affected scope indicator if applicable
  - Severity chip

5) Footer actions (context dependent)
- If entered from “apply” flow: Back / Confirm and continue
- If entered from “rollback” flow: Back / Confirm rollback
- Always: Copy diff as text, Download JSON, “Open in API” link

Diff visualization patterns
- Default: side-by-side comparison (Old / New) for readability with structured configs.
- For boolean toggles: compact switch-like representation (OFF → ON) with short helper text.
- For numeric fields: show delta badges (e.g., “+32” or “×2”) when meaningful.
- For enums: show old/new pills.
- For lists/maps: show added/removed items with +/- markers; allow expand to raw JSON.

Risk model (UX)
We need consistent visual severity that matches semantic validation logic.
- High risk (red): likely to cause outages, major latency regressions, or quality regression (quant). Examples:
  - Quantization profile change (any) without passing quality gate
  - Disabling KV/prefix cache for high-throughput routes
  - Increasing max batch size beyond safe ceiling for model/hardware profile
  - Enabling experimental kernel / scheduling policy flagged “beta”
- Medium risk (amber): can change performance/cost noticeably; may be safe but needs canary.
  - Adjusting target batch latency window, cache TTL changes, aggressive prefill settings
- Low risk (blue/gray): metadata changes or minor thresholds within safe ranges.
  - Minor batching heuristic weights, logging toggles (non-PII), annotations
- Informational (gray): reorder-only changes, cosmetic changes, no effective delta.

Important: risk is determined server-side (ENG-4822 semantic validation) and returned per-field. UI should not try to infer risk on its own, but can apply a fallback mapping by field path when risk metadata is missing (for older versions).

“Expected impact” callouts
Goal: provide operator guidance even if they don’t know what a field means.
- Callouts should be sourced from validation output where possible:
  - “This change is expected to increase throughput at the cost of p99 latency.”
  - “This config is incompatible with model X on A10; may increase 5xx.”
  - “Quant profile change requires eval gate: score must be within threshold.”

UI behavior
- If impact is unknown or missing: show “Impact: Unknown” and prompt to run canary.
- If multiple changes contribute: show a combined impact summary + per-field explanations on expand.
- Provide a “View gates” link that jumps to gate configuration and current evaluation status (if in a rollout context).

Edge cases to handle
- Partial rollout diffs: when ‘Active’ differs by shard/region due to canary
  - UI should show a banner: “Active config varies by rollout shard” with a link to the rollout page.
  - Diff view should allow selecting “Compare candidate to active (majority)” vs “Compare candidate to baseline (pinned)” (v1: majority only).

- Schema changes across versions
  - Missing field in old version: show as Added
  - Removed field: show as Removed
  - Renamed fields: show as Removed + Added (v1); later we can support rename mapping.

- Large diffs
  - Provide “show only changes” toggle (default ON)
  - Provide search by field name/path
  - Collapse unchanged groups

- Permissions
  - If user lacks permission to view full config: show redacted values with clear labeling (e.g., “hidden due to policy”). Still show that a value changed + risk/impact summary.

Copy requirements (ties to DES-213)
- Warning banner copy must be unambiguous and action-oriented.
- Avoid implying guarantees. Use “expected/likely” language.

Acceptance criteria
- Can compare any two Optimization Config versions and see:
  - A summary of changes with risk breakdown
  - Scope chips and version metadata
  - Per-field diff grouped by category with old/new values
  - Expected impact callouts (when available) and a graceful ‘unknown’ state
- High-risk changes are visually prominent above the fold.
- Diff can be copied/exported for incident notes.

Open questions
1) What exact structure comes back from semantic validation for per-field risk and impact? (depends on ENG-4822)
2) Do we need “effective config” preview per model worker when there are overrides? (likely later)
3) For Private: do we show raw JSON paths exactly as Helm/Terraform values? Or keep control-plane schema as source of truth?

Artifacts / links
- Drive: rollback UX notes + open questions (see shared drive doc: rollback-ux-notes-and-open-questions)
- Confluence: Optimization Config versioning design spec (optimization-config-versioning-design)
- Eng tickets: ENG-4822 (diff + semantic validation), ENG-4828 (Console history/diff endpoints)

Deliverable
- Figma file with:
  - Diff view page template
  - Components: risk summary strip, risky changes list, grouped diff table, copy/export affordances
  - Redaction states, empty states, schema mismatch states

Handoff notes (for Console eng)
- Prefer server-provided “diff items” with: path, label, old_value (string), new_value (string), risk (enum), impact (short string), category, is_effective_change (bool).
- UI can render old/new as plain text with an “expand raw” for long JSON.
- Summary counts should be computed server-side for consistency.


comments:
2025-09-24 (Paula Mendes): Creating design ticket to complement DES-211 (history UI). Diff view is the key to preventing scary ‘apply blind’ moments. Priority P1 since it blocks safe apply UX review.
2025-09-30 (Kenji Nakamura): First wireframes in Figma: header w/ scope chips + version metadata, summary strip w/ risk counts and impact callouts, then ‘Risky changes’ pinned section. Need confirmation from Eng on which fields will have risk metadata vs fallback mapping.
2025-10-03 (Chloe Martin): +1 on pinned risky changes section. Also request: diff must be usable from rollback modal (read-only, with emphasis on what we revert *to*). Please ensure page supports ‘Compare candidate to active’ quickly from rollout flow.
2025-10-07 (Jordan Lee): Semantic validator will emit per-path severity + message. We can provide a combined impact summary, but in early versions impact may be ‘unknown’ for many fields except quant profile and max batch size ceilings. Recommend UI treat impact as optional.
2025-10-09 (Sean Gallagher): On-call feedback: show scope and blast radius in the header (tenant/model/region) with big typography. During incidents, mis-scoping is the #1 fear. Also add ‘Copy diff as text’ for postmortem notes.
2025-10-14 (Kenji Nakamura): Updated designs: ‘show only changes’ toggle default ON, search by path/label, collapsible categories. Added banner for partial rollout states (‘active varies by shard’).
2025-10-18 (Paula Mendes): PM review: approved. Please align wording with DES-213 for confirmation copy and avoid guarantee language in impact callouts.
2025-10-21 (Kenji Nakamura): Final handoff complete. Added redaction state for RBAC-limited viewers and schema-mismatch empty states. Marking Done.
